body:
Reviewed all 63 pages of the immutable diff (head d556ead): the new portable relationship contract trio (law/shape/domain `relationships.cljc`), the byte-identical `frontmatter.cljs→.cljc` rename, the new domain/shape test suites plus the portable JVM+CLJS contract runner, the 7-gate `eta-mu-review.yml` workflow with its 8 GiB hosted disk reserve, and the planning cards, ledger events, and `.ημ` verification corpus.

Deterministic evidence: `summary.json`/`deterministic.log` show success at the exact head with all gates at status 0 (diff stat/hygiene, install, source dependencies, lint, test, build). Historical failures retained in the evidence artifacts (RED runs, the initial bootstrap cwd miss, the first hosted run that omitted source-deps bootstrap) are honestly documented observations, not failures introduced at this head.

Findings: none confirmed. One candidate — the unreachable `:malformed-uuid` guard in `admit-update` (relationships.cljc:207), verified dead because `valid-mutation?` rejects every blank/nil uuid first — was classified rejected: the observable behavior remains a classified atomic refusal with no partial admission, which is what the contract and tests require. The prior review's tie-ordering defect at this file is independently re-verified as fixed (the `pr-str` final sort component distinguishes `nil` from `""` uuids, pinned by permutation tests on both hosts), and the cycle-analysis missing-target NPE path is unreachable because reference errors short-circuit before cycle analysis.

Non-blocking notes: (1) test gap — the workflow's 125-skip branches are unexercised by any in-repo test; (2) test gap — the JVM leg of `relationship_contract_runner` is not part of `pnpm test` (it runs in the evidence corpus only); (3) the retained read-board projection RED (parent/epic/dependency/type dropped) is documented, executed, and explicitly scoped to the incoming writer story — not a regression of this change; (4) deleting or pinning the dead `:malformed-uuid` branch would remove the intent/behavior mismatch.
